text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000115 bills 99215 at a nearly flat rate across patient complexity, including healthy patients, but the documentation sample is too thin to confirm or refute upcoding.","leaning":"pattern_consistent_with_upcoding","interpretation":"The claims pattern does not look like a sicker panel. The 99215 share stays at about a quarter for patients with 0, 1 or 2 chronic conditions, far above peers at each tier, and most 99215s fall on low-complexity patients. Sampled examples include single routine diagnoses such as J06.9 (C0058177, C0058391), N39.0 (C0057485) and I10 (C0057522), which would rarely support high-complexity decision-making. The documentation does not confirm this: the few documented 99215s were all supported, and some were high-complexity patients (for example C0058134). With records for only about 3% of claims and just 5 documented 99215s, the charts are too thin to judge either way, and the 3 moderate-plus data-reviewed notes without a lab or test line are only weak hints of templated notes. A reviewer should first request charts for the low-complexity 99215 claims listed (for example C0057485, C0058019, C0058420) and check whether the MDM and time in those notes reflect the visit or appear cloned."}
